analysis:
Reviewed fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (head lines 1-2004). This is a test-vector fixture, not runtime code. The visible head content contains canonical request, provider body, template input, plan and token-id vectors for one model, including the harmony-framing, tool-turn, endpoint-mapping and block-boundary cases. The patch excerpt shows an "additional_context": {"enable_thinking": false} field added to a template_input, plus changes to prompt_token_count, chain_hash and block_boundaries (for example 803 -> 767, with the 768-token block dropped). The patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed regions (head about 3020-3926, 43739+, 52354+) fall outside the supplied units, so those hunks were not verified directly.

Security relevance: the vectors feed prompt-contract IDs and block chain hashes, which relate to the prefix-cache and cross-tenant sharing threat (T-041, TB-007). The contract ID is unchanged (8171fec3...), while chain hashes changed in a non-visible region. The source of the change cannot be assessed from this fixture alone. Visible content contains only synthetic data, with no secrets or real user data. Test-only content does not alter authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior (TB-002, TB-009).

Remaining integration questions: the unseen implementation changes (the Swift/Go prompt rendering and plan hashing that consume these vectors) should be checked for consistency. In particular, chain-hash domain separation and scope_id binding should still hold when enable_thinking is injected, and cache-routing eligibility should not be widened. No evidence of a regression in the supplied lines.
